claims.statement: apps/api/finance owns ingestion, categorization, dashboard reads, the chat agent, and evals; apps/web is the browser and never opens Postgres; supabase/migrations owns the schema.
import_statement is the only writer of new ledger rows: it detects a BBVA or CaixaBank PDF, resolves the account by IBAN, and inserts transactions with on conflict (dedup_key) do nothing.

Import does not categorize. POST /imports returns after the insert and schedules categorization in the background; the CLI runs categorization after a successful import and still reports categorization failures separately.

The production cascade pairs own-account transfers, applies enabled system rules, then asks jev one call with three typed questions, resolves merchants, and sets needs_review when jev category confidence is under 0.95 or merchant resolution drops the name.
Cascade saves never overwrite category_source user, a failed jev row stays pending, and one process-wide lock serializes background categorization runs.
After categorization saves, link_loans attaches each unmerchanted loan row to the merchant of its contract number, preserving a merchant already linked by that rule step.

User labels and merchant confirms live outside the cascade: a transaction label sets category_source user, and confirming a merchant relabels only jev, merchant, or none rows and records them as user labels, which are the golden set.
finance seed upserts categories, category_groups, and rules from supabase/seed YAML and disables rules removed from that YAML; migrations do not load it.
Dashboard aggregates read only v_transactions_enriched through one shared filter, and a month with no imported data is has_data false rather than zeros.

The chat is one create_agent ReAct loop with a single run_sql tool. It is disabled, and chat routes return 503, when the database URL is missing or an xAI model has no XAI_API_KEY; other API routes keep working.

Every agent query is checked as one SELECT over the transactions and subscriptions views, then executed as agent_reader in a read-only transaction with search_path agent; those views project v_transactions_enriched and v_subscriptions without ids, IBANs, or raw descriptions.
At chat startup the YAML semantic layer is checked against the live agent views, and every metric and example is guarded and EXPLAINed; a mismatch fails startup.
The LangGraph checkpointer is the agent's memory and can be rewritten by summarization, while chat_threads and chat_messages are the UI history and do not shrink.
finance eval-categorization dry-runs the production cascade against user labels, ignores merchant defaults, writes no ledger rows, and appends one line to docs/evals/HISTORY.md.

The everyday shell row is MAIN_ITEMS (Overview, Transactions, Subscriptions, Chat, Review). MORE_ITEMS (Imports, Settings) render in more-menu.tsx from lg and in the mobile sheet below lg. Spending, income, and merchant routes are reached from views, not from the nav, and pages call the API rather than Postgres.
public tables have no row-level security; this is a single-user local app, and jev and the chat model receive cleaned text and agent-view rows but not an IBAN or description_raw.

Merchant resolution merges a new name into a known merchant at merge_threshold 0.5 inclusive, and from merge_suggestion_floor 0.3 inclusive up to that threshold it creates the new merchant and records a review suggestion. Inclusive boundaries are locked by test_merge_and_suggestion_thresholds_are_inclusive.
GET /imports returns every import with no row cap, ordered by period_end descending nulls last, then account name, then imported_at descending. The /imports coverage board reads that whole list.

Settings reads accounts, categories, and GET /dashboard/group-slots. Account rename is the only write; category names are shown as stored and are not editable from the page. Group slots come from the same group_slots function the overview uses.
